jobs.title: Product Manager [Summer 2027 Intern] at Saja
jobs.description: Employer: Saja Expires: 11/08/2026 About SAJASAJA is building a new way to collect, trade, and engage with physical collectibles through a digital-first experience. We're looking for a Product Management Intern for Summer 2027 to own a piece of the product and see it through.What you'll doOwn a project for the summer that ships and matters to the product.Figure out what problem you're solving before deciding what to build.Write things down clearly enough that engineers and designers aren't guessing.Look at how people actually use the product, where they get stuck, and where they leave.Define what success looks like before your project ships, then be honest about the numbers afterward.Talk to users, read support tickets, and spend real time in the product yourself.What we're looking forClear thinking and clear writing. Most of this job is making a fuzzy problem legible to other people.Comfort with data. You don't need to write SQL, but you should be able to look at numbers and work out what they do and don't tell you.Something you've organized, built, or run where you had to make decisions and live with them. A club, a project, an event, a side product.Curiosity about why people behave the way they do, and the instinct to check your assumptions rather than trust them.Willingness to do the unglamorous parts, including support, QA, and writing copy.Interest in consumer products, marketplaces, gaming, collectibles, fintech, or e-commerce.Currently enrolled in a degree program and returning to school after the internship.What this internship is actually likeAt our size, product work is less about process and more about owning a problem until it's solved. You'll write specs, but you'll also chase bugs, answer users, and pull numbers yourself. You'll have someone senior to work through decisions with, and you'll see the effect of what you build quickly, including when it doesn't work.You do not need prior PM experience or a background in collectibles. We care much more about how you think, how clearly you communicate, and whether you finish what you start.For our interview process: Must have a US-based App Store account.Please do not apply to multiple roles within Saja. We will automatically consider you for other roles, but please only apply to one role.

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Communications, Brennan en Español Undergraduate Internship at The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law School
jobs.description: Employer: The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law School Expires: 11/08/2026 The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU School of Law is a nonpartisan law and policy institute that seeks to improve the systems of democracy and justice in the United States. We work to hold our political institutions and laws accountable to the twin American ideals of democracy and equal justice for all. The Brennan Center’s work ranges from voting rights to campaign finance reform, from ending mass incarceration to preserving constitutional protections in national security policies. Part think tank, part advocacy group, part cutting-edge communications hub, we start with rigorous research. We craft innovative policies. And we fight for them — in Congress and the states, in the courts, and in the court of public opinion. We are seeking interns to join our Communications department on the Brennan en Español team to provide research / writing, and administrative support to staff. Note: This internship is in-person at our New York City office. Responsibilities: All interns will assist with general research and administrative work for the Brennan Center, including coordinating meetings, and drafting routine correspondence. Additionally, there will be opportunities to attend and observe substantive meetings, events, and conversations on program work. In addition to administrative duties, specific responsibilities for the BEE department include: Helping the BEE team with research for different projects, including our newsletter. Writing social media messaging and assisting with social media posting. Contributing to videos for our social media platforms, including helping with writing scripts, and editing and recording of videos. (Experience on-camera is a plus but not required.) Monitoring both coverage in the Spanish-language and Latino press, and announcements and events by Latino organizations. Fluency in both English and Spanish is required. A video assessment will be requested for candidates selected to move forward in the hiring process. Qualifications: The ideal candidates are independent self-starters; detail-oriented; energetic; punctual; and highly organized. Interns must also have excellent research, writing, and analytical skills, as well as a passion for our issues. Experience with Windows, Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Word is a must. Database experience is very helpful. Applicant must be open to evolving responsibilities. We are committed to considering a wide range of candidates, including those with diverse experiences and backgrounds. If you're uncertain about meeting 100% of our qualifications, we encourage you to apply anyway.In your cover letter, please share your interest in the position and what you hope to contribute to the role. This internship is only open to undergraduate students in Spring 2027. Hours: Approximately 10-20 hours per week Pay: $18.40 per hour Duration: Spring Semester 2027 Application Deadline: November 23, 2026 Note: The Brennan Center will follow the rules of your school regarding internships. Therefore, if a school doesn’t allow you to do a paid internship for some reason (i.e., receiving credit, etc.), then your internship will not be paid. In addition, if you are participating in a formal school internship program that allows you to work more than our stated hours, we will make a determination based on our needs and further assessment of your school’s program. To Apply:Please >>LINK HERE<< and upload (preferably in pdf) your (1) resume, (2) cover letter, (3) and a list of contact details for supervisor references. In your cover letter, please specify what interests you about the Brennan en Español team and the Brennan Center for Justice Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage interested students to apply early, as the position will be filled once qualified candidates are found. No phone calls, please. If you have difficulty with the online system, you may send your application by e-mail to brennancenterjobs@nyu.edu with “Spring Brennan en Español Internship” in the subject line, after registering in the online system. Applying through our website is strongly preferred.

jobs.description: Employer: Genuine Parts Company Expires: 11/09/2026 Job DescriptionJob Summary Are you ready to spend your summer as a part of something special? Opportunity Sizing Model that estimates potential inventory reduction, turn improvement, and profitability benefits. Interactive Dashboard allowing users to explore opportunities by category, supplier, store, and distribution hub. Executive Opportunity Ranking highlighting the highest-impact assortment optimization opportunities across the business. Final Leadership Presentation summarizing key findings, recommendations, and next steps. Preferred Qualifications 3.25 GPA or above preferred. Leadership Skills Embodies the following values: serve, perform, influence, respect, innovate, team. Effectively communicates by motivating and inspiring others through clear and proactive communication. Delivers results and drives customer success by committing and focusing on outcomes to deliver results and making the customer the center of decisions. Makes balanced decisions and thinks strategically by being a forward thinker. Physical Demands / Working Environment Expected to operate in a professional office environment. jobs.title: Marketing and Communications Intern - Report Launch at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 11/09/2026 About The Autoimmune FundAutoimmune and immune-mediated diseases affect millions of people, most of them women. Yet the money has gone almost entirely one way. Of the $40.0 billion in venture funding that went to the field from 2014 to 2025, 94.4% went to drug therapeutics. Prediction, diagnostics, devices, care access, monitoring and remission maintenance shared the remaining 5.6%. The Autoimmune Fund, a seed and Series A venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, exists to back the rest.In December we publish The Autoimmune Decade: Investing Across the Immune Economy, our annual report on the field. It launches during JPM Healthcare Week in January 2027, the biggest week of the year for healthcare investing. Your job is to help make sure the right people read it. What You'll DoYou'll report directly to the fund's Managing Partner and work across the full launch.Run the content calendar. Write, schedule and track LinkedIn posts, short-form copy and email from now through launch. Find out what lands, then do more of it.Build the launch audience. Research and organize lists of investors, health system leaders, patient advocates and press. Keep them clean, tagged and ready to use.Support partner and event outreach. Draft invitations and follow-ups, track RSVPs, and prepare briefing materials for launch events.Get the report into hands. The report is free to anyone who wants it. Help run distribution and track who requests it.Be there for launch week. Possible travel to San Francisco during JPM Healthcare Week, with travel and lodging covered. You HaveCurrent enrollment in an undergraduate programA strong writing sample. You write clean, fast copy that doesn't sound like a press releaseSocial or campaign experience for a club, organization, startup or your own account, with results you can showReal organization under deadline: calendars, trackers, follow-up that doesn't slipHands-on AI use for drafting, research and repurposing contentExactness with numbers. You copy figures precisely and ask before roundingAvailability onsite in Los Angeles through January 2027 Nice to HaveCoursework in communications, journalism, marketing, public health or the life sciencesInterest in healthcare, biotech or women's health, or a personal connection to autoimmune diseaseEvent experience, including student-run eventsCanva skillsExperience with an email or CRM tool such as Mailchimp or HubSpot What You'll GetDirect mentorship. You work side by side with the fund's Managing Partner, a clinician and former Wall Street healthcare equity analyst who covered 500+ companies over 14 years.A real launch on your resume. Not a class project. A public report with real partners and a hard deadline.A network. Exposure to investors, founders and advocates during healthcare's biggest investing week.Proof of results. Posts, campaigns and numbers you can point to in your next interview. To ApplySend your resume, two writing samples (at least one short-form, such as posts or captions), and a short note (150 words max) about one campaign or post you ran: what you expected, what actually happened, and what you changed to bonnie@autoimmune.fund. Work Test (2 to 3 hours, unpaid)We'll send you a two-page excerpt of our findings.1. Write three LinkedIn posts in three different formats (for example, a single striking number, a short story, a question). Each under 150 words.2. Write a 100-word email inviting a senior healthcare investor you've never met to a launch event.3. Show your sources. List every number you used and quote the exact line in the excerpt it came from.4. Flag what's wrong. The excerpt contains at least one error. Find it and tell us how you'd handle it before posting.

jobs.description: Employer: ONE Carmel Expires: 11/09/2026 ONE Carmel is an 891-acre private community in Carmel Valley, framed by the Santa Lucia Mountains and the Pacific, with 73 estate homesites across the property. Alongside the real estate business, ONE Carmel is developing a program of exhibitions, performances, artist residencies, and gatherings that connect the community to the creative life of the Monterey Peninsula. About the internship This is a rotational internship for a current undergraduate who wants to see how a small, ambitious organization actually runs. You will rotate through the executive office, the arts and culture program, marketing and communications, and community and sales operations over the term. You will work closely with the CEO and his Executive Assistant, sit in on real meetings, and take ownership of a project that matters to the business. What you will do Executive office - Support the CEO and Executive Assistant with research, scheduling, meeting preparation, and follow-up. - Draft briefing notes, summaries, and correspondence for review. - Help maintain the contact database, filing systems, and project trackers. Arts and culture program - Assist with planning and day-of logistics for exhibitions, performances, salons, and community events. - Research artists, galleries, and cultural institutions and help build partnership outreach lists. - Help catalog and archive artworks, program materials, photography, and press. Marketing and communications - Draft social media, newsletter, and website content that reflects ONE Carmel's voice. - Assist with photography, video, and content capture at events and on the property. - Track press coverage and compile simple reports on audience and engagement. Community and sales operations - Support property tours, homeowner communications, and visitor hospitality. - Help prepare materials for prospective buyers, partners, and civic stakeholders. - Take on a term-long project of your own, agreed in your first two weeks, and present it to the team at the end of term. Who this is for - A current undergraduate (sophomore, junior, or senior) in any major; art history, arts management, business, communications, real estate, hospitality, or environmental studies students may find an especially natural fit. - Curious about art, design, architecture, land, or community. - A clear writer and careful communicator, comfortable speaking with adults you have just met. - Organized and reliable. - Comfortable with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365; Canva, Adobe Creative Cloud, Squarespace, or CRM experience a plus. - Able to reach the work location on a regular schedule with a valid driver's license. - Eligible to work in the United States. What you will get - Direct exposure to a CEO and leadership team. - Hands-on experience across four functions in one term, and a completed project. - Mentorship, mid-term and end-of-term reviews, and a reference on successful completion. - Paid work in one of the most beautiful settings on the California coast, scheduled around classes. Compensation Paid internship at $22.00 per hour for 10–20 hours per week during the academic year, flexible around classes, with the option to extend. Academic credit paperwork available where your program allows. Mileage for approved off-site errands is reimbursed.

jobs.title: Chemistry Research Intern (2027) at Indiana Biosciences Research Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Indiana Biosciences Research Institute Expires: 11/10/2026 IBRI is poised to transform life sciences—and for millions of people, even life itself.The Opportunity:The IBRI is seeking motivated undergraduate or graduate students for our Summer Internship Program. Interns will gain hands-on experience in a dynamic research environment, working alongside scientists and professionals on active projects that contribute to real-world scientific advancement.Program Dates: May 17, 2027 – August 6, 2027Application Deadline: Applications will be accepted through November 30, 2026. For priority consideration, apply by October 15, 2026.Schedule: 35 hours per weekStipend: This internship includes a stipend of $9,650 for the full program, disbursed in bi-weekly installments on or before the 7th and 22nd of each monthResponsibilities: Assist with lab experiments, sample preparation, and data collection.Review scientific literature and summarize key findings.Record results clearly using lab notebooks and digital tools.Help analyze data and prepare charts, figures, or short summaries.Join team meetings, trainings, and scientific discussions.Follow lab safety, biosafety, and ethical research practices.Qualifications:Enrolled in (or recently graduated from) an Indiana university undergraduate and/or graduate program OR having graduated from an Indiana High School.Degree in a field related to biology and/or chemistry.Strong interest in scientific research.Excellent organizational and communication skills.Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team setting.Interested in pursuing graduate studies or a career in research or science policy.Commitment to the full duration of the internship.Familiarity with software such as Excel, R, Python, or statistical tools (preferred).Basic understanding of laboratory techniques and data analysis tools (preferred). About Us:The Indiana Biosciences Research Institute (IBRI) is a first-in-class translational medicine institute dedicated to advancing life sciences in the race to eliminate disease and improve human health and life.By connecting early-stage biotech companies with cutting-edge life science discoveries —and backed by the mission and resources of industry leaders, investors, and philanthropic partners—IBRI is successfully evolving a new, independent model to conquer disease, uniting previously fragmented forces in the quest for cures.Carefully curating and supporting early-stage companies with investment, talent, and space, IBRI strategically accelerates drug discovery. Our work benefits from the relatively low cost of living and doing business here, allowing more resources to be directed toward science.Fueled by the same entrepreneurial creativity as the groundbreaking scientific work we support, IBRI’s labs advance research across the frontiers of diabetes, metabolic disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and rare pediatric diseases. Our ambitious public–private vision cultivates talent while efficiently bridging the gap between research-driven inquiry and profit-driven drug development.At IBRI, cures are launched on a clear pathway to clinical trials, enabled by the combined resources and experience of our academic and industry partners, without the typical pressure to deliver rapid results for commercialization. IBRI labs pursue breakthroughs that might never happen elsewhere. Breakthroughs are happening here. Our novel financing model ensures that when discoveries are ready for clinical trials, the intellectual property is sold back to industry or spun off, creating a direct stream of revenue.By every measure, the IBRI model demonstrates a novel approach that delivers rewards. Scientific bench work is nurtured, drug discovery is advanced, workforce development is continuous, investors see returns, and donors see impact. Most importantly, IBRI’s structure and portfolio of accomplishments matter to the patients whose lives are improved—or even saved—by this forward-looking approach to life sciences.IBRI is driven to bring next-generation therapies to market with an understanding of the complex pressures that often bind innovation to economics. After more than a decade, the evidence is clear: IBRI is poised to transform life sciences—and for millions of people, even life itself.Equal Employment Opportunity:The IBRI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and does not discriminate based on age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 11/10/2026 Have you ever thought about the sophisticated supply chains that are needed to deliver consumer products to the store shelves for our consumers? And how do companies negotiate services contracts needed to support the infrastructure, employees, and marketing? We believe excellent ideas emerge from the creative connections that happen between our hardworking employees, and we encourage diverse, multi-functional teams to work together to generate new ideas to address challenges we face. P&G has positions available at various technical centers and plants (including Cincinnati) across the United States. Purchasing internships are 12-week paid engagements. We believe that this provides the right opportunity for building a strong foundation for future growth potential. As a purchasing intern you will own decisions on how to source and/or handle the product flows which are the backbone of our company. You will communicate with & closely partner with different internal functions daily. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1. jobs.title: Systematic Fast Trading Intern at Man Group
jobs.description: Employer: Man Group Expires: 11/10/2026 The TeamMan Systematics’ Fast Trading Strategies (FTS) team is responsible for the development of high Sharpe, high-frequency trading strategies across all asset classes. The team has been running for over a decade and currently manages a large and successful portfolio across both global futures and cash markets. The FTS team is responsible for the full end to end development of the fast alpha portfolio, using several techniques to capture fast alphas, ML, event driven, microstructure based etc, building its own customized monetization stack, and optimizing trading and order placement with dedicated high-frequency infrastructure.This posting is specifically for candidates interested in interning in the New York office, which houses Man Systematics’ business unit focused on high-frequency alpha research, trading, and infrastructure.Who Should Apply?The team is currently hiring PhD students for an MLE/QR internship with strong academic achievement in highly technical degree programs who are interested in a summer internship (expected to be between 10 – 12 weeks).Candidates are encouraged to submit only one application using their university email address via the below link, which requires a resume that includes all completed and in-progress post-secondary education GPAs. School transcripts may be optionally provided immediately or later in the process.Kindly note that our summer internships are open to penultimate year students only.Purpose of the RoleThe MLE role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about software that is focused on machine learning applications such as MLOps and research workflows. Because MLEs are also expected to use their own software, the ideal candidate not only has experience coding in a variety of languages (especially Python) but also has knowledge of ML algorithms and research processes.The QR role is ideal for individuals who are passionate about using high frequency tick data and machine learning algorithms to predict asset returns and converting those models into profitable trading strategies. QRs will work closely with MLOps in deploying models and therefore are required to be strong programmers in a variety of languages (especially Python). Previous ML or statistical research internship experience in finance, technology, or academia is strongly preferred.Working HereMan Systematic fosters a performance driven, meritocratic culture with a small company, no-attitude feel. It is flat structured, open, transparent, and collaborative, offering ample opportunity to grow and have enormous impact on what we do. We are actively engaged with the broader research and academic community, as well as renowned industry contributors.We’re fortunate enough to have a modern high-rise office in central Midtown conveniently located near Central Park and continually strive to make our environment a great place in which to work.We have annual away days and research off-sites for the whole team.We open-source some of our technology. See https://github.com/man-groupWe regularly talk at leading industry conferences, and tweet about relevant technology and how we’re using it. See @manquanttech and @ManGroup.Our Oxford lab is collocated with the Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance (https://bit.ly/36goTic) and the Machine Learning Research Group in Engineering Science, University of Oxford (https://bit.ly/2MSHDwy)

jobs.title: Engineering Co-Op: Spring 2027 at Safran Electrical & Power
jobs.description: Employer: Safran Electrical & Power - Safran Electrical & Power Expires: 11/11/2026 We're looking for students interested in working hands-on on real engineering projects. We offer Spring, Summer, and Fall rotations in a handful of areas (see below for more info). Our goal is to bridge the gap between classroom and real experience. Our hope is for students to feel like the work they're doing is valuable whilst challenging. Depending on a candidate's specialties and assigned area, roles require the following: Passion for mechanical, electrical, computer, or aerospace engineering, manufacturing, and technology. Strong analytical ability to solve problems and ability to learn quickly. Strong written & verbal communication skills to generate process instructions and reports. Ability to follow a structured project management process including document meeting minutes, action items, and monitor progress. Capability and tenacity for solving unique engineering problems. Ability to learn quickly and a desire to keep improving skills and to teach others when possible. Team player with a highly proactive and positive attitude with ability to work on own or in a team as needed. Hands-on skills. Demonstrated interest in building and testing. Regular, predictable attendance is required. Please note that estimated time for start/end dates are based on Spring 2027. Other semesters will have different dates. Want to know more about each of our Area Assignments? Let our managers tell you! Conversion Engineering: The Conversion Engineering Team is responsible for controller-generators and starter-generators (as well as converting the power they produce). We design and support multiple products with our current new product introduction (NPI) programs. The Mechanical Engineering Team designs the housings and assembly methods for our systems, ensuring they meet strict environmental and operational requirements. Their work is essential to delivering robust and reliable solutions for our aerospace applications. Embedded Systems Engineering: If you're curious about how hardware and software come together to power real-world systems and are eager to make an impact while learning from experienced engineers - join our Embedded Systems Engineering team. Industrialization Engineering: Industrialization is the perfect blend of design and manufacturing work. We have a mix of both in reviewing engineering drawings, discussing design features, developing solutions, mitigating design risks, managing prototype builds, building tooling, and implementing new products into production. We get the benefit of working with every department in the business and every day is different. If you want to have a mix of design work behind a desk and time on the production floor seeing designs you helped create come to life - then Industrialization is right for you! Manufacturing Engineering: As a Co-Op, you will work directly with our production team and design engineers to support the assembly and troubleshooting of aircrafts power-conversion units. We perform root-cause analysis on units that fail functional testing, remove roadblocks for our production team, diagnose defective parts, improve assembly processes, update work instructions, and initiate corrective actions. If you want hands-on experience on the shop floor and to improve efficiency while reducing waste - apply for Manufacturing Engineering. Production Support Engineering: Working in Production Support Engineering you will have the opportunity to work on real products and support day-to-day engineering activities that directly impact production, product reliability, and customer satisfaction. Responsibilities may include assisting with failure investigations, supporting resolution of production and supplier-related issues, evaluating nonconforming hardware, participating in repair and overhaul activities, reviewing engineering documentation, and contributing to engineering changes that improve product performance, manufacturability, and long-term supportability. Project Management: Everything starts with an idea, and project managers bring ideas into reality. From managing and executing plans, creative problem solving, and balancing the needs and expectations of a cross-functional team; project managers touch every aspect of the business and the world around us. With Project Management at Safran you will get real world understanding of how products and projects come to life, leveraging the strength of the team and how to manage risks and budget along the way. Quality Engineering: If you're looking to help ensure customer satisfaction and promote continual improvement of our products and processes, then the Quality Team may be for you. Our team is responsible for maintaining our Quality Management System (QMS), facilitating Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and conducting internal quality audits. We promote continual improvement in the form of corrective actions and improvement projects. Rotating Machines Engineering: The mechanical design team within the Rotating Machines Department excels in engineering robust and high-performance aircraft rotating machinery. This includes generators and starter-generator systems. This group specializes in designing critical mechanical components such as rotors, stators, shafts, bearings, splines, and housings to ensure reliability and efficiency under demanding aerospace conditions. Supply Chain Engineering: Supply Chain is where ideas are transformed into finished products. We partner closely with suppliers to secure everything the business requires—from engineering components to the materials, equipment, and services that support daily operations. You'll gain firsthand experience in turning plans into reality by collaborating with suppliers, resolving challenges, and ensuring materials flow efficiently throughout the process. Systems/ Analysis Engineering: The System Integration & Performance Team develops, integrates, and validates aerospace electrical power systems by bringing together hardware, software, and control systems into a complete solution. Team members support system testing, performance analysis, troubleshooting, and certification activities to ensure products meet customer and regulatory requirements. Test Engineering: The Test Engineering Team specializes in test design, execution, and reporting for all power units. The team is composed of both test engineers and test equipment engineers. The test engineers handle the design, setup, execution, reporting of research and development testing, and qualification testing of new products and/or systems. Meanwhile, the test equipment engineering team design mechanical, electrical, and control equipment for the test lab to enable both production and new product testing to take place. Through Life Support Engineering: The Through Life Support Engineering team works on the problems that happen after designs enter production. The team investigates failures (both in the field and on the production line), solves production and supplier issues, supports repair and overhaul activity, evaluates nonconforming hardware, manages obsolescence, and develops design and drawing changes that keep products operating safely and reliably throughout their service life. For Co-Ops, it is a great opportunity to work on real hardware, see how engineering decisions affect the entire product lifecycle, and gain hands-on experience through a wide variety of technical challenges compared to working on a piece of a long-term development program.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Internship Program - Office of Employee Benefits (Finance and Accounting) at Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Expires: 11/11/2026 As an employee of the Atlanta Fed, you will help support our mission of promoting the stability and efficiency of the U.S. economy and financial system. Your work will affect the economy of the Southeast, the United States, and the world. The work we do here is important, and how we do it is just as important as what we do. We live our values of integrity, excellence, and respect every day. We do the right thing, we do things right, and we treat people right. A career at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta gives you the chance to do work that touches lives and helps communities prosper. OUR BANK - The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States and is one of the most influential, trusted, and prestigious financial organizations. It consists of twelve Reserve Banks located around the country and the Board of Governors in Washington, D.C. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta territory covers the Sixth Federal Reserve District, which includes Alabama, Florida, and Georgia, and portions of Louisiana, Mississippi, and Tennessee. The Atlanta Fed and the other Reserve Banks play an important part in all three of the Fed's functions: monetary policy, bank supervision and regulation, and the operation of a nationwide payment system. PLEASE READ:Internships are paid. Summer housing will not be provided. This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, performance standards or requirements, efforts, skills or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different tasks be performed when circumstances change (e.g. emergencies, rush jobs, change in workload or technological developments). The Office of Employee Benefits (OEB), located in Newark, N.J., comprises a staff of 64 professionals who oversee benefit programs for approximately 80,000 current and former employees of the Federal Reserve, and their beneficiaries. The OEB was established in 1934 to administer the Federal Reserve System’s Retirement [pension] Plan. Over time, the OEB's responsibilities have expanded to include additional retirement benefits, health benefits, life insurance, long-term disability, and other personal protection plans. The OEB's mission is to be a center of excellence, providing leadership in formulating employee benefit programs and operating these programs on behalf of the Reserve Banks, Board of Governors and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau with outstanding customer service, sound and cost-efficient operations, professional expertise, and ongoing innovation. Summer finance intern at the OEB will be placed into the Finance and Accounting Department and will be involved in projects supporting retirement plans, health and welfare program as well as budget assignments.The program is extremely competitive, and size is limited. As a summer intern at the OEB, applicants must have a demonstrated interest in business, finance, benefits, human resources, information systems, legal, compliance, communications or a related discipline and a strong academic record. Specific skills may be required depending on area and project. This program is open to rising juniors pursuing a bachelor’s degree. Responsibilities:• Hands-on accounting experience• Live reconciliations, journal entries, and applicable financial reporting and general ledger work• Practical applicable of controls (COSO and ICOFR)• Support automation efforts through testing and build (projects) Qualifications:• Working knowledge of MS Excel, MS Word, MS PowerPoint; • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills demonstrated by the ability to assimilate new information, make sound decisions, and manage multiple tasks; • Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and written; • Ability to grasp information quickly; • Attention to detail; and • Ability to work productively in a high-performing, collegial atmosphere. Please include resume, cover letter and unofficial transcript. You should indicate your work area(s) of interest in your cover letter. CORE COMPETENCIES:Proficient in Microsoft Office SuiteExcellent communication skills (verbal and written)Strong analytical skillsAbility to work independently and take ownership of projectsGreat work ethic and detail orientedComfortable working across time zones to complete projects in a timely manner OUR BENEFITS TO INTERNS (some benefits are subject to being onsite):Professional development opportunitiesNetworkingFree LinkedIn Learning accessFree access to our FedFuel career development toolDress for your dayFlexible hours TO APPLY:In addition to your application, please attach a resume and a copy of your most recent unofficial transcript. Additional Requirements: This position will require at minimum fingerprinting for a criminal background check, education and employment verification, along with potential additional screening requirements due to the information accessed while performing the job. Any offer of employment is contingent upon satisfactory results of any required background screening. These screenings would be initiated at the time of offer acceptance and can take up to approximately 8 weeks to be completed. The screening covers areas such as education/employment verification, criminal history, credit history, and reaches out to your references and people that know you well. For Law Enforcement positions, physical, psychological, drug, stress/EKG, and attending an academy will be required. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta employees must comply with the Bank’s ethics rules. These rules generally prohibit employees, their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children from holding financial interests (such as common stock and corporate bonds) issued by financial institutions. This prohibition also applies to investment funds that focus on investing in the financial sector. If you, your spouse/domestic partner, or minor child own such securities, you will generally be asked to divest them if you accept an offer of Bank employment. If you have concerns about this prohibition, you should raise the issue with the recruiter for this posting early in the process. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Financial Services Sales Program, Internship at Northwestern Mutual - Orange County
jobs.description: Employer: Northwestern Mutual - Orange County Expires: 11/11/2026 OverviewThe Financial Services Sales Program is a paid, 12-week early-career experience where students have an opportunity to explore the path to becoming a Northwestern Mutual Financial Representative. Through comprehensive training, personalized coaching, mentorship, and real client-facing experience, you'll develop foundational sales, relationship-building, and communication skills while exploring whether an entrepreneurial advisor career is right for you. In this hands-on program, you'll operate as an independent contractor, learning how financial advisors help clients navigate important financial decisions by understanding their goals, identifying their needs, and creating personalized financial plans. You can build a go-to-market strategy and business plan, learn how advisors conduct client conversations about financial goals and needs, and understand how they help guide individuals toward solutions tailored to their needs. Along the way, you'll see how advisors earn trust, develop lasting client relationships, and recommend insurance, investment, and wealth solutions that support a client's broader financial goals. Unlike many traditional internships, this program is built around real responsibility and practical application. You'll learn through experiencing and doing, not just observing. Our goal is to provide a depth of experience that helps you build valuable professional skills, understand what it takes to grow a business, and make a meaningful impact in the lives of others. By the end of the program, you'll have a clearer understanding of the advisor career path and the opportunity to determine whether it's the right fit for your future.Schedule: Flexible, designed to work around classes and other commitments Compensation: Up to $3,000 in activity-based pay, plus commission on sales. There is no salary or hourly compensation.ResponsibilitiesWhat You'll Learn Develop Career-Ready Skills Through Real Experience: Build communication, sales, relationship-building, and business development skills through hands-on training, coaching, mentorship, and real client interactions. Learn How to Help Clients Plan for What Matters: Gain exposure to Northwestern Mutual's planning approach and learn how insurance, investments, retirement planning, and other solutions can help clients achieve financial security. Explore an Entrepreneurial Career with Clarity: Get experience learning how business development, client relationships, accountability, and compensation contribute to long-term success. What You'll DoIn the Financial Services Sales Program, you'll: Develop foundational sales skills through hands-on client interactions, including hosting discovery conversations to understand their priorities and goals.Build a market of potential clients through prospecting, personal connections, referrals, and new relationships. Learn about Northwestern Mutual's holistic financial planning approach and how advisors develop recommendations across insurance, investments, retirement, and other financial decisions. Work alongside experienced financial advisors through mentorship and joint work opportunities. Secure required Life, Accident & Health insurance licensing By completing the available training in this program, including holding the College Agent’s Contract, meeting licensing requirements, building your network, conducting discovery conversations, participating in client planning activities, applying coaching feedback, and engaging in business development, you will be better positioned for success in this program or whatever career you may choose. How Compensation WorksCompensation is tied to completing sales- and business-focused program activities, including conducting financial discovery conversations and learning how advisors prepare personalized recommendations. Additional compensation takes the form of commissions from eligible sales. Here's how it works: You can earn up to $3,000 during the program based on completing sales and business development activities You also have the opportunity to earn commissions from sales There is no salary or hourly compensation QualificationsWho This Early-Career Program Is For We're looking for students who are: Currently enrolled full-time in college (juniors and seniors preferred) Interested in learning about financial planning, business development, entrepreneurship, or sales Comfortable building relationships and starting conversations with others Motivated by personal growth and professional development Able to independently manage priorities, responsibilities, and accountability Curious about exploring the financial representative career through direct experience rather than observation aloneEligible participants may be considered for a full-time financial representative role following graduation. Participants may also be considered for another role within their local network office
